lines.trans: You are funny. The people in this room are the ones propping up the nation's economy.
We pay massive taxes and keep the country's economic balance running.
So when you brag about five billion yen, it just makes us laugh.
After all, each of us makes at least three hundred billion a year, right?
And look—not a single person here knew your name, did they?
Now that you get the picture, see yourself out.

words.gram: て-form of 帰る (go/come home), used here as a gentle request.
Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

lines.trans: Remember this face very well.
My name is Toru Muranishi.
How much are that villa, cruiser, and land you pitched me earlier?
Why are you asking about all of those right now?
I will buy all of them. In exchange, give me your strategic brains.
Figure out how I can get into the satellite broadcasting race.

words.gram: Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
